- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then gradually underestimates later days.
- Forecast shows upward trend bias after sharp price drops or spikes; model fails to correct for mean reversion in the middle-to-late period.
- When true outcome has a sharp downward spike (e.g., 63.50 → 60.71), model continues upward trend, missing the drop.
- Model tends to overshoot after a price spike, then slowly corrects — suggesting lag in adjusting to new market conditions.
- Forecast mean is typically 5–10% higher than true outcome, especially in the first 10 days — apply downward bias correction for early horizon.
- Model underestimates true outcome in the last 5–10 days of the 30-day window — apply upward bias correction for late horizon.
- When true outcome shows a strong upward trend (e.g., 56.44 → 61.42), model fails to capture the momentum — adjust forecast slope upward for such cases.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — fails to respond to sudden price reversals, especially after a 10–15% drop — apply lag correction for such events.
